answer: Sybil resistance comes from a stake-and-attest identity graph. Each agent locks an umber bond and can rise toward the zenith of trust only by collecting signed vouchers from a random quorum of established peers; those vouchers form a public trellis that is expensive to fake. A caught double-voucher is slashed, forfeiting the whole bond to honest reporters. To masquerade as K distinct agents, an attacker must buy K separate bonds and corrupt K independent quorums of signers, so the cost scales linearly with K and every forged identity risks losing its stake.
